PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve multiple pending steering messages
PullRequest.Body:

### current behavior before this pr

only the latest steering message is shown

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a611c3f5-6306-4970-aa27-2514136082f7


### with this pr

all steering messages are shown

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6e7dc91-7903-488b-9c73-731cfc1dc720


### chatgpt app (reference behavior showing multiple steering messages)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4bc0b9ba-72f7-466c-9725-9008a5767df0






## Problem

Sending a second steering message while Codex is working hides the first pending message, even though the model may receive both.

In the before-fix reproduction, the user asks for five timed shell calls and sends steering messages while Codex works. Only the last one, `say baz`, remains visible, but the assistant replies:

> foo bar baz. Continuing the timed sequence.

AHP's single steering slot replaces each earlier message. Codex can still have those messages buffered, so the pending UI no longer reflects what was sent.

<!-- Add the before-fix VS Code and ChatGPT app recordings here. -->

## Fix

Use the AHP 1.1.0 steering-message list from [microsoft/agent-host-protocol#512](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/512). Adding B keeps A visible. Consuming A removes only A.

- Keep each message's attachments and sender, and deliver it once the provider is ready. Independent messages no longer use Copilot's replaceable startup buffer.
- Match Codex receipts by submission ID, including identical prompts. Keep text matching for older servers and clear failed Copilot submissions without creating a successful turn.
- Preserve the legacy slot. With an older host, later submissions wait locally until the slot clears. Old clients see their slot and normal output, not the new pending list.

This PR pins AHP commit `57241b5a`. Land the protocol change first and refresh the pin against the accepted upstream version.

## Tests

The original regression failed for Codex, Copilot, and Claude configurations. The fix covers both the new list and older-host fallback, with each message visible until consumed and sent once.

After merging `main` at `3b486b1ff92`, **108 focused tests pass**, including steering and the built-in Ask agent URI test. Client build, type-check, and targeted lint pass.

These are client, host, and provider-boundary tests. The recordings show the bug before the fix; live-model UI verification of the fix and full product smoke tests were not run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop and its Copilot call path are explicit: every retained entry calls sendSteeringMessage, which launches sendSteering; sendSteering always awaits _reconcileMcpServerEnablement, whose sequenced body unconditionally invokes rpc.mcp.listConfigured. The only magnitude uncertainty is how many messages users or agent-to-agent callers accumulate during a long preparation window and the runtime latency of that local RPC.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Copilot SDK RPC calls and concurrent steering tasks, including attachment conversion work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A deferred batch of N independent steering messages performs N serialized rpc.mcp.listConfigured IPC calls before the N required sends; attachment conversion and SDK sends can then overlap N-way.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Avoidable IPC and head-of-line latency delay later steering messages after provider readiness, with additional CPU/I/O pressure when messages include attachments.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: During preparation the legacy steering slot retained only one replaceable message, so readiness flushed at most one Copilot steering operation and therefore one MCP reconciliation/listConfigured RPC from this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: When provider readiness follows turn preparation, the host now releases every retained steering entry by starting a separate provider operation. For Copilot, each operation independently runs MCP enablement reconciliation before sending.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 208 is inside the newly added loop over every pending independent steering message and invokes provider.sendSteeringMessage once for each entry. Before this diff, _syncPendingMessages handed the provider only the single replaceable state.steeringMessage slot.
Findings.Title: Coalesce provider preflight when flushing deferred steering
Findings.Impact: After a user or agent queues several steering messages while Copilot is preparing or refreshing configuration, the kth message cannot reach the SDK until repeated MCP-list RPCs ahead of it complete; larger bursts also launch multiple attachment conversions and sends concurrently once their preflights clear.
Findings.Evidence: QueueDrainContribution lines 195-208 iterate state.steeringMessages and call sendSteeringMessage for each unsubmitted entry. CopilotAgent.sendSteeringMessage starts target.sendSteering without awaiting it; CopilotAgentSession.sendSteering always awaits _reconcileMcpServerEnablement, and lines 5248/5253 serialize that reconciliation through _mcpEnablementSequencer while unconditionally calling session.rpc.mcp.listConfigured. Thus an N-message deferred list causes N avoidable, serialized IPC preflights even though all entries share the same session configuration.
Findings.Recommendation: Add a batch/provider queue boundary that performs MCP reconciliation once when a deferred list is released, then submits the independent messages in order (or coalesce concurrent reconciliation onto one in-flight promise) while retaining per-message IDs and completion handling.

Scenarios.Scenario: A current client submits several steering messages while a Copilot turn is preparing, then provider progress makes the turn ready.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each client action must be accepted and retained; on readiness QueueDrainContribution synchronously releases every unsubmitted entry. Each Copilot task then waits for its own MCP reconciliation before its SDK send, so the serialized reconciliation RPCs are on the steering-delivery critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot SDK rpc.mcp.listConfigured, plus enable/disable RPCs if configuration differs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N listConfigured RPCs for N deferred steering messages; additional MCP mutation RPCs depend on configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preparation retained one replaceable legacy slot, so readiness caused at most one reconciliation from this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The sequencer places these N RPCs ahead of the corresponding SDK sends, delaying later steering messages.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read resource contents for selection-style attachments and convert message attachments
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to the total attachments across N messages; conversions can overlap across the N launched tasks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the single retained preparation-time steering message reached this work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Attachment conversion must complete before each SDK send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One required send per accepted independent message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the latest message survived the preparation-time legacy slot, although messages submitted after readiness could already each send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each message is delivered through this boundary after its preflight.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct pending steering IDs accumulated during preparation; no grouping reduces N before provider handoff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: QueueDrain starts N Copilot sendSteering tasks without awaiting. Their MCP reconciliations serialize through _mcpEnablementSequencer, after which attachment conversion and SDK sends may overlap N-way.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SubmittedSteering deduplicates accepted provider handoffs, but deferred entries are retried. MCP reconciliation has no warm-result cache or in-flight coalescing: every steering task executes rpc.mcp.listConfigured, including warm sessions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed loop, uncached preflight, sequencer, and provider boundary are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical manual bursts may contain only two or three messages and local SDK RPC latency varies; agent-to-agent steering and unusually long preparation windows can produce larger N.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: required per-message sends are accompanied by avoidable per-message serialized MCP preflight RPCs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Independent steering is submitted to ready Codex or Claude turns and later consumed by provider echoes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The state action is reduced, QueueDrain hands each new entry to the ready provider, and provider acceptance/echo emits a per-ID removal. These steps are on delivery and pending-UI clearing paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per independent message, N total.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preparation retained only one slot, while already-ready messages could already be sent individually.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to deliver each message; requests are launched without host-side serialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue priority-now SDK messages for the Claude provider stream
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued SDK message per independent steering entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the replaceable legacy slot was represented in host state during deferred periods.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Enqueue is synchronous; downstream provider transport handles delivery off this immediate host path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N steering messages during one active turn, generally a small user-entered list but also reachable from session server tools.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Codex starts one turn/steer JSON-RPC request per entry without a shared limiter; Claude enqueues entries into its existing SDK pipeline and drains them through its iterable queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SubmittedSteering and provider pending maps deduplicate IDs after acceptance. There is no delivery cache; cleanup removes IDs on echo, failure, abort, turn promotion, or chat disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cardinality and lifecycle; insufficient evidence of a separate actionable regression beyond the Copilot preflight finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No repository evidence establishes problematic Codex transport limits for realistic steering counts; Claude explicitly queues rather than bursts the boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: one provider call per independent message is required by the feature, Codex count is normally small, and Claude already queues delivery.

Scenarios.Scenario: A steering message contains embedded or snapshot attachments and is accepted through the host protocol.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before state reduction, AgentService detects rewritable attachments and awaits all per-message attachment rewrites; the resulting resource references are retained until the provider consumes the message.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist embedded/snapshot attachment payloads under the session attachment root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One rewrite operation per rewritable attachment across accepted messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The rewrite path already existed for turns and legacy pending messages; this PR extends it to each independent steering action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action is not reduced or delivered until its rewrites complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Attachments per steering message and number of independent pending messages.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Attachments within one message use Promise.all; separately dispatched messages follow the service's action sequencing while provider conversion may overlap later.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Snapshot files are created per submitted attachment; no cross-message content cache is used. Pending-state cleanup releases message references, while normal attachment-root lifecycle owns files.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the filesystem path, but the operation is required to preserve attachment semantics and no duplicate rewrite of one action was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Attachment-bearing steering is less common than text-only steering, and payload sizes are not bounded by evidence inspected here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: work scales with distinct submitted attachment payloads and is not shown to repeat beyond required per-message processing.

Scenarios.Scenario: The workbench projects pending steering lists during live actions, restoration, reconnect, and legacy-host fallback.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Local pending-request changes are diffed into protocol actions; host acknowledgements and remote state changes are projected back into the chat model. Legacy hosts expose only the slot, so later local messages wait until it clears.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch set/remove actions over the agent-host protocol
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One set per new independent message and one remove per local cancellation; deduplication prevents repeated sends while awaiting projection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Modern clients used a single replaceable steering action; older-host fallback remains one-at-a-time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Set acknowledgement is required for authoritative host retention, but local pending UI remains visible while in flight.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize steering list in negotiated snapshots/replay and filter it for legacy clients
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list of N entries per relevant chat snapshot; live updates remain incremental actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Snapshots contained only the optional single steering slot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Snapshot serialization is on initialize/reconnect, not per-token rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pending requests P and protocol steering entries N for one chat; reconnect snapshots include N entries only for negotiated clients.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Client action dispatch is ordered by the protocol connection. Legacy fallback deliberately serializes one steering slot; modern list actions are independent but state projection remains synchronous on each state change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: LocalSteeringSubmissions suppresses redispatch before acknowledgement and is deleted with the chat subscription. Protocol capability projection strips the list for unsupported clients; reconnect uses snapshot/replay state rather than refetching external data.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for state and protocol paths; low evidence of user-visible cost at realistic N.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large pending lists are atypical; UI diffing has some quadratic searches but realistic N is small and no hot rendering loop was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: deduplication and lifecycle cleanup are present, legacy delivery is serialized, and snapshot/list processing is bounded by pending-message count.

Scenarios.Scenario: A session server tool steers an active target session multiple times.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each tool invocation dispatches a ChatSteeringMessageSet into the target chat and returns after state dispatch; QueueDrain then performs provider handoff as in direct client submissions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch host state and eventually invoke provider steering transport
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One state action and one required provider delivery per tool call, plus Copilot's per-entry MCP preflight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A second steer was rejected while the single slot was occupied; this PR accepts multiple independent entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The tool response follows state dispatch; provider delivery continues through side effects and can lag behind due to serialized Copilot preflights.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tool-generated steering calls targeting the same active chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tool invocations create independent entries; effective provider concurrency follows Copilot/Codex/Claude behavior described above.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Message IDs are unique and retained until consumed; SubmittedSteering prevents duplicate handoff after acceptance. There is no grouping of multiple tool calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for reachability and per-call cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Model/tool invocation rates are workload-dependent, but this path can create larger bursts than manual typing.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported Copilot preflight fan-out; no separate provider-independent issue is established.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 36 changed files and traced modern/legacy client submission, host state reduction, attachment rewriting, queue drain, Copilot/Codex/Claude delivery, server-tool steering, UI projection, reconnect, and cleanup. One medium-confidence-severity performance regression was submitted: deferred Copilot lists fan out into N uncached serialized MCP configuration RPCs before the N required sends. No performance-fix learning record applies because the PR addresses correctness rather than a proven shipped performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
